title: Predictive KV eviction and contiguous slab allocation for cross-plane batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads we observe increased KV cache fragmentation and cross-plane memory churn when tensor and pipeline parallelism interact. This causes elevated tail latency, sporadic OOMs on older hardware, and suboptimal spill behavior.

Goal: Implement a predictive eviction policy combined with a contiguous-slab allocator and cooperative cross-GPU slab merging to reduce fragmentation, reduce cross-plane communication during KV rebalancing, and improve tail latency under continuous batching. The design targets minimal runtime overhead and compatibility with existing spill-to-host and prefetch paths.
acceptance_criteria: Tail latency (P95/P99) for chat and streaming workloads decreases by at least 12% compared to baseline under identical QPS and sequence length distributions
Total per-GPU KV memory fragmentation reduced (measured as unusable free / total KV capacity) by >= 25% in synthetic fragmentation tests
No increase in average per-request CPU overhead > 5% vs baseline; added background threads bounded
System handles sustained continuous-batching workloads for 24h with zero OOMs in our medium cluster perf job
All changes gated behind runtime flags and pass integration tests for spill/prefetch and cache correctness
implementation_plan: Design: finalise eviction predictor model (hybrid LR + token-hit histogram) and contiguous-slab allocator API (shard-aligned slab headers)
Prototype: implement predictor in kv-manager with shadow metrics for 1 week; implement contiguous-slab allocator with fallback to existing allocator
Coordination: add crossplane slab-merge RPC with safety barrier and idempotent reconciliation; ensure compatibility with tensor-slice layouts
Prefetch/Spill integration: extend async prefetcher to request slab ranges rather than individual microshards
Testing: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration perf job (medium cluster), chaos tests for GPU removal and slab reconciliation
Rollout: canary on dedicated pools (5%) -> increase to 25% after 48h -> full rollout after perf signoff
Cleanup: remove experiment flags and prune shadow code after 2 successful release cycles
benchmarks: Prototype run (2026-03-09): 10% P99 reduction in a 64-GPU mixed tensor/pipeline job (seq=1024, QPS scaled to 80% peak). Baseline: 182ms P99, prototype: 164ms P99
Fragmentation sim (2026-03-11): baseline unusable free 18.2% vs allocator prototype 11.8%
Memory overhead: prototype metadata + predictor adds ~1.9% per-GPU memory usage in worst-case
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictor misclassification could evict hot keys causing QoS regressions. Mitigation: conservative safety margin + shadow mode before enabling eviction actions; replicate hot keys to a small hot-slab ring
Risk: Crossplane slab-merge window could introduce stalls. Mitigation: use asynchronous handover with non-blocking copy + atomic pointer swap and limit merge size per epoch
Risk: Increased complexity in allocator could make debugging harder. Mitigation: extensive telemetry, slab-level tracing and deterministic replay harness for allocator operations
